analysis.title: Amkor Technology Inc. (AMKR): Weaker smartphone and consumer results offset strength in computing and advanced packaging
key_insights: Goldman expects AMKR to trade in a range after a tepid 3Q26 with revenue and EPS guidance below the Street, against sharply lowered expectations going into the print.

Investor positioning had become more muted ahead of the quarter because of ongoing smartphone weakness, despite optimism around the CPU program ramp, the expanded Nvidia partnership and phase 2 of the Arizona campus.

3Q26 revenue was $1.99bn versus GS at $2.05bn and Street (Visible Alpha) at $2.01bn. Gross margin was 18.3% versus GS 19.5% and Street 19.1%. Operating margin was 11.3% versus GS 12.5% and Street 12.1%. Operating EPS was $0.76 versus GS $0.82 and Street $0.78.
By end market in 3Q26 QoQ: Communications down 8%, Computing up about 25%, Automotive and Industrial up about 7%, Consumer up about 10%.
Management narrowed 2026 CapEx to $2.5bn and expects spending to stay elevated in 2027, peak in 2028-29 and normalize after, driven by Arizona Phase 1 tool spend and Phase 2 construction.
Amkor does not expect to take on incremental debt in 2027, supported by customer prepayments from existing partnerships.
Arizona is expected to run at a cost premium to Korea because of labor and building depreciation. Strong utilization, favorable product mix and more automation should narrow the gap over time.
The FY27 CapEx framework is unchanged: about 15% of $12bn for Arizona, $4.0-$4.5bn for Korea and about $50mn for Vietnam.
Computing is guided up low double digits QoQ and more than 50% YoY in 4Q, driven by 2.5D-related revenue and the CPU program ramp, which more than offsets weakness in PCs and laptops.

Customers are making long-term capacity commitments and advance payments. Pricing is expected to offset higher substrate and material costs. Advanced packaging growth is expected to accelerate in CY27, with no specific targets given.

Consumer revenue rose about 10% QoQ on IoT and home electronics. Management guides a mid-teens QoQ decline in 4Q, well below typical seasonality, as memory and other component shortages constrain consumer electronics demand.
Management said visibility into CY27 smartphone demand is limited and it is too early to give an outlook.
4Q26 guidance midpoint: revenue $1.95bn (GS prior $2.07bn, Street $2.00bn), EPS $0.65-$0.75 with midpoint $0.70 (GS prior $0.84, Street $0.73), gross margin up about 20 bps at the midpoint.
GS cut 2026E-28E EPS to $2.52 / $2.50 / $2.80 (from $2.70 / $2.70 / $2.90) on a modestly lower growth outlook.
GS cut its 12-month price target to $56 from $65, using 22x P/E (down from 25x) on unchanged normalized EPS of $2.60. Rating stays Neutral.
GS sees limited upside until Amkor shows stronger operating leverage or greater scale in 2.5D packaging, and wants better gross margin expansion and cash flow before turning more constructive.

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut to $56 from $65 as the P/E multiple falls to 22x from 25x on slower growth assumptions. Neutral is kept because AI/HPC packaging tailwinds are offset by weak operating leverage and cash flow.

sector_views.rationale: AI/HPC-driven 2.5D packaging demand and a second-source role for advanced computing products support Amkor's computing growth.
Smartphone visibility into CY27 is limited and memory and component shortages are constraining consumer electronics demand, with Consumer guided down mid-teens QoQ in 4Q.

earnings_insights: AMKR 3Q26 reported revenue $1,991mn vs GS est $2,046mn and Street (Visible Alpha) consensus est $2,014mn, with growth of 18.2% QoQ and 0.2% YoY.

AMKR 3Q26 operating EPS reported $0.76 vs GS est $0.82 and Street consensus est $0.78. Gross margin reported 18.3% vs GS est 19.5% and Street est 19.1%. Operating margin reported 11.3% vs GS est 12.5% and Street est 12.1%.

AMKR 4Q26 guidance: revenue midpoint $1.95bn (range $1.90-2.00bn) vs GS prior est $2.067bn and Street est $2.006bn. Operating EPS $0.65-$0.75, midpoint $0.70, vs GS prior est $0.84 and Street est $0.73. Gross margin midpoint 18.5% vs GS est 19.6% and Street est 18.8%. Net income midpoint $173mn vs GS est $211mn and Street est $184mn.

GS revised estimates (new vs old): 2026E revenue $7,556mn vs $7,695mn, operating EPS $2.52 vs $2.70. 2027E revenue $8,600mn vs $8,759mn, operating EPS $2.50 vs $2.70. 2028E revenue $9,343mn vs $9,573mn, operating EPS $2.80 vs $2.90.
GS forward quarterly operating EPS estimates: 4Q26E $0.73, 1Q27E $0.69, 2Q27E $0.65.
risk_factors: Upside risk: better-than-expected volumes in the 2.5D packaging business.
Upside risk: better gross margin leverage from utilization of new production facilities.
Downside risk: failure to execute on the 2.5D packaging roadmap.
Downside risk: failure to execute on new smartphone design wins.
Memory and other component shortages are constraining consumer electronics demand.
Elevated CapEx through 2028-29 and Arizona's cost premium to Korea weigh on margins and cash flow.
vol_and_positioning: Investor positioning in AMKR was muted going into the print because of smartphone weakness, and expectations had been lowered significantly.
GS expects the stock to be range bound after the print.

tension_points.theme: AMKR advanced packaging vs weak consumer
tension_points.bull_case: Computing is guided up more than 50% YoY on 2.5D and the CPU program, customers are making long-term capacity commitments and prepayments, and advanced packaging growth is expected to accelerate in CY27.
tension_points.bear_case: Smartphone and consumer demand is weak with 4Q Consumer guided down mid-teens QoQ, 4Q revenue and EPS guidance are below the Street, and operating leverage, gross margin expansion and cash flow have yet to show improvement.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS says it would turn more constructive on evidence of stronger operating leverage or greater scale in 2.5D packaging.

theme_stances.key_argument: Amkor benefits from AI/HPC-driven advanced packaging tailwinds, but GS wants stronger operating leverage, gross margin expansion and cash flow before being more constructive.
theme_stances.evidence: we would prefer to see stronger evidence of sustained operating leverage
